title: Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024
book_use: Chapters 1-3: global weighted-average utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell from USD 0.417/kWh in 2010 to USD 0.043/kWh in 2024; 452.1 GW of solar PV was added in 2024; distinguish LCOE, installed cost, capacity, and delivered-system cost.

title: Electricity 2026 — Supply
book_use: Chapter 1 and later framing: solar PV generation growth and forecast milestones through 2030; forecasts are scenario-dependent and must be dated rather than stated as inevitabilities.

title: Solar Achievements Timeline
book_use: Chapter 1 historical anchor for practical silicon PV development in the 1950s and early commercial milestones; use as timeline context rather than a complete global history.

title: World Energy Investment 2025 — Executive Summary
book_use: Chapter 2: approximately USD 450 billion of solar investment in 2025 and roughly USD 400 billion annual grid investment; supports the claim that generation capital is scaling faster than network investment.

title: Crystalline Silicon Photovoltaics Research
book_use: Chapter 2: silicon remains the dominant PV absorber and modern modules are manufactured semiconductor products; use for technology background, not project economics.

title: Renewables 2025 — Renewable Electricity
book_use: Chapters 3-4: solar PV dominates projected renewable-capacity growth; rising variable-renewable shares increase the importance of flexibility, storage, curtailment management, demand response, and grid investment.

title: Renewable Power Generation Costs in 2024
book_use: Chapter 3 and planned Chapter 5: utility-scale battery storage installed costs fell sharply from 2010 to 2024; treat duration, chemistry, location, financing, and application as important system boundaries.

title: Building the Future Transmission Grid — Executive Summary
book_use: Chapter 4 and planned Chapters 11-13: IEA tracked around 1,650 GW of advanced solar and wind projects waiting for grid connections in 2024; queue capacity is not equivalent to projects certain to be completed.

title: Grid Investments
book_use: Chapter 4: electricity demand growth increases the need for grid expansion and modernization; energy efficiency can substitute for part of generation/network expansion but does not eliminate grid needs.

title: Building the Future Transmission Grid
book_use: Chapter 4 and later bottleneck chapters: transmission expansion faces supply-chain, procurement, permitting, and component constraints; use as evidence that wires and equipment can become the pacing item after generation gets cheaper.
